Date: Wed, 08 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 comp band recalibration and offer guidance

Team —

Following up from our compensation review workshop last week, attached is a proposed recalibration of base salary bands and geo multipliers for levels IC3 through L6. High-level notes: 

- Benchmark set: market medians from CompBench (2025 Q3) + 25 enterprise SaaS comps we track.
- US coastal tech markets have moved ~6–8% above last year; midwest/remote continues to compress toward national medians.
- Proposed changes: tighten band widths at senior levels, raise midpoint for L5 by 7% in US, introduce a regional multiplier table (EU: 0.92, APAC: 0.78 for Singapore/SE Asia, 0.72 for India).
- Hiring guidance: offers should target 90–110% of midpoint depending on experience and sign-on realities; sign-on sizing guidance included per level in the sheet.

Ask: please review and confirm (a) approval to publish updated bands next Monday 10/13, (b) whether we should accelerate any L5/L6 counter-offer buffers for ongoing offers, and (c) headcount impact on Q4 hiring budgets — Markus, can you confirm runway to absorb the midpoint increases?

Attachments: 2025-10-08_geo_band_proposal.xlsx

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Total Rewards
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Q4 comp band recalibration and offer guidance

Laura —

Thanks for the thorough write-up and spreadsheet. Quick reactions:

- The L5 midpoint bump feels justified based on candidate feedback from recent offers.
- Agree on tightening band width at L6; reduces negotiation friction.
- For active offers (4 total across Eng and Infra), recommend we allow a one-time ad hoc buffer up to +7% of midpoint if needed — but require a hiring manager justification form.

Markus — does the CFO view allow the one-time buffer and the overall uplift to go live on 10/13? If not, what compromises (e.g., smaller geo uplift or delayed implementation) would you propose?

Vivek
VP Engineering

Subject: CompBench Q3 2025 — key takeaways for Redwood
To: Carrie Moss <carrie@compbench.co>

Hi Carrie —
Attached is the regional break-out we ran for Redwood's peer set. Highlights called out for discussion:

- Senior ICs (L5/L6) have the largest upward movement in the bay and NYC markets; 75th percentile up ~9% YoY.
- Small-medium enterprise SaaS companies are leaning more toward equity-heavy packages at higher levels — if Redwood keeps equity target steady, cash uplift is constrained.
- APAC variance is large; Singapore is closer to EU medians while India remains ~30% lower.

Suggested action: adopt the proposed EU multiplier but stagger APAC multipliers by country group (Singapore/HK: 0.9, SE Asia: 0.78, India: 0.68). Also consider a mid-cycle equity refresh for L5+ to keep total comp competitive without escalating cash base.

Attachments: comp-bench-report-2025.pdf

--Carrie Moss
Principal, CompBench Consulting
carrie@compbench.co

Subject: Re: Q4 comp band recalibration and offer guidance

Thanks everyone — good discussion and helpful data from Carrie. Quick decisions and next steps: 

1) Approve publishing updated bands on Monday 10/13 with the following adjustments: EU multiplier set to 0.92; APAC split into Singapore/HK (0.90), SE Asia (0.78), India (0.68).
2) Approve a temporary +7% one-time buffer for active offers at L5 (requires hiring manager justification ticket + HR approval). HR to log each instance in HR-TICKET-1427.
3) Markus: please confirm budget reallocation by EOD Fri 10/10. If runway is constrained, we will delay the rollout for L6 until Jan 2026.
4) Laura/Marissa: update offer templates, the hire pack checklist, and the compensation decision log. Link the published bands in the offer letter template and note the effective date.
5) Carrie: thanks — we'll incorporate your staggered APAC proposal; please send a short memo (1–2 pages) summarizing the suggested equity refresh framing for L5+.

I'll post the finalized band workbook to the Drive folder and send a follow-up summary to managers once Mark's budget confirmation is in.

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
